steps.say: Different texts have different features. Features help you know what kind of text you are reading.
Information texts have a title, subheadings and facts. Some have a Did you know? box.
Instructions have a list of things you need and numbered steps. The steps start with bossy verbs.
Poems are often written in verses, and many have rhyming words.
Playscripts show the speaker's name and a colon. Stage directions go in brackets.
steps.show: AMIR: (worried) I can't find my book.

steps.say: Letters have an address, a date, a greeting and a sign-off.
steps.show: Dear Grandad, ... With lots of love, Bima

check.prompt: Which text would have numbered steps?

options.why: Poems are written in lines and verses.
Letters use paragraphs, not numbered steps.

hints: Numbered steps tell you what to do, in order.
Which text tells you how to make something?
check.explanation: A recipe is a kind of instructions, so it has numbered steps to follow in order.
